title: Compound interest
teach: With compound interest, interest is added each year and the next year’s interest is worked out on the new, bigger amount: interest on interest. A = P(1 + i)ⁿ, where i is the rate as a decimal and n the number of years. Compound interest = A − P.

ex.q: R5 000 is invested at 8% compound interest per year. Find the amount after 2 years.

watch:
10% for 3 years compound is not 30%: 1,1³ = 1,331, so it is 33,1%.

Problem-solving lens
Make a year-by-year table first; then check it against the formula.

qs.text: R5 000 at 8% compound interest for 2 years. Find the amount.
qs.steps:
1. Formula (compound interest): A = P × (1 + i)ⁿ, where P is the starting amount, i is the yearly rate as a decimal and n is the number of years.
2. A = 5 000 × 1,08²
3. = 5 000 × 1,1664 = R5 832

qs.text: R2 000 at 5% compound interest for 3 years. Find the amount.
qs.steps:
1. Formula (compound interest): A = P × (1 + i)ⁿ, where P is the starting amount, i is the yearly rate as a decimal and n is the number of years.
2. A = 2 000 × 1,05³
3. = 2 000 × 1,157625 = R2 315,25

qs.text: R4 000 at 10% compound interest for 3 years. How much interest is earned?
qs.steps:
1. Formula (compound interest): A = P × (1 + i)ⁿ, where P is the starting amount, i is the yearly rate as a decimal and n is the number of years.
2. A = 4 000 × 1,1³ = 4 000 × 1,331 = R5 324
3. interest = R5 324 − R4 000 = R1 324
